item.title: We don't need no education platform evolution. Hey, Redmond, leave those kids alone
item.description: "Give me the child until he is seven, and I will give you the man." This saying about the importance of influence in early education is variously attributed either to St Ignatius of Loyola, founder of the Jesuits, or Aristotle, depending on whether you wanted to entrust your very young son to Catholic priests or ancient Greeks. Fortunately for both groups, perhaps, neither of them ever said that, even though both certainly believed it. Another group that certainly believes it is the cadre of tech company policy makers, which goes a long way to explain the cultural and legislative backlash to what happens to young people online. The least pernicious and longest established example of the catch 'em young principle is the educational discount for hardware and software. Apple has been the highest profile company to do this, with hardware discounts and aggressively positioned complete service packages for educational institutions, often integrated with funding authorities. If you grow up using a package or platform, it becomes your first tech language and you're likely to become a lifetime customer. Microsoft has also played this long game, seasoned where it can with curriculum integration. Its latest wheeze, described by the company as educational platform evolution is a response to institutions' changing needs, with clearer pathways to adopting and enabling new technologies. Yada, as we say, yada. The evolved platform removes email and Teams from the free student tier, while imposing the requirement for Windows hardware to qualify, along with comprehensive restructuring of higher tiers and storage not necessarily to the advantage of the educators. This is the same sort of evolution to evolving needs as the British Empire brought to natives of other lands. Hello, India. Greetings, Africa. Whassup, America! These warships packed with gun-toting Brits are here to evolve your changing needs in local resource management. Microsoft has realized what Imperial Great Britain adopted as its primary principle. If you can get your future, ahem, customers over a barrel, then not only can you imprint your brand on their minds, you can take their money. You have to come up with some balderdash to cover it, whether it's about civilization and progress or enabling educators to… oh God, these poor fingers can't even type this stuff. Missing completely is the idea that educators' evolving needs may not include spending even more money on basic necessary services when budgets are stretched tight. Moreover, while existing uses of the old tier can stay on it until the end of next year, new sign-ups have to be on the Enhanced Speedy plans. Keen students of history, especially those in the former colonial lands of Eastern North America, may care to refresh their memories of events some 250 years ago. It is quite natural, when being bent over a barrel ceases to be an amusing pastime, to seek a less barrel-shaped position. In this case, the pressure to find alternatives has

Lastly, The Nation reports that the All Progressives Congress (APC) and the National Democratic Congress (NDC) have clashed after the latter accused the former of excessive spending and priotising campaign over serious issues of governance. item.title: Wunmi Adelusi: Why Are We Still Hiding That We Use AI?
item.description: Not long ago, I finished a piece of writing I was proud of — my thoughts, my argument, my structure. I had used an AI tool to help tighten the grammar and smooth the flow. And then, before sharing it, I went hunting through the text to delete every long dash. Why? Because the em dash has become the internet’s favourite “tell” that AI was involved. I was, quite literally, editing my work to hide a tool I had every right to use. When I caught myself doing it, I had to laugh. And then I had to ask: why the shame? It turns out I am not alone. Across a study spanning 47 countries, 57% of employees admit to concealing how they use AI at work. The reasons are almost entirely about reputation. In one recent survey of 5,000 desk workers, nearly half said they worried about appearing less capable or less competent, and a third feared they would simply look lazy. We are using the tools, and quietly scrubbing the fingerprints. There is even a quiet hypocrisy to it. Another survey says out of 7,200 adults, 46% said they would not disclose AI’s role in their own work while the remaining 54% said other people should. I had assumed this reticence was a particularly African trait. In my own experience, my colleagues in DC and Europe — my manager included — are refreshingly matter-of-fact about it. In one meeting recently, when asked to find a specific document in a shared folder, my manager cheerfully said he’d just let AI search it rather than disturb anyone’s work. Someone joked about his “secret agent,” and we all laughed. It was open, unbothered, upfront. I had concluded that we, of African descent, were simply more conservative, more inclined to glorify the heavy lifting, to wear “I stayed up all night doing it myself” as a badge of honour. But the research corrected me. This isn’t cultural; it’s universal. Employees across the US, UK, Europe, Latin America, Japan and Australia hide their AI use at strikingly similar rates. Even leadership does it. In some studies, managers conceal their AI use more than junior staff do. So perhaps the real question is why do we treat AI-assisted work as less credible than work done the hard way? I’ve even heard of recruiters downgrading CVs that look AI-generated, penalising the polish itself. But surely the more useful question is whether the substance behind it is real. A candidate who used a tool to sharpen how they present genuine experience hasn’t cheated; they’ve shown resourcefulness. The due diligence should be on verifying the claims, not on detecting the dashes. Screening out the tell, rather than testing the truth, risks rejecting capable people for the crime of being efficient. Because when you think about it, the logic is backwards. Using AI well is not a shortcut that replaces thinking; it is a skill that reveals it. You cannot get something excellent out of these tools without putting something substantial in. item.title: Manufacturing growth doubles to 3.2% amid easing cost pressures
item.description: By Yinka Kolawole Nigeria’s manufacturing sector recorded a 3.2 per cent year-on-year (YoY) growth in the second quarter of 2026, up from 1.6 per cent in the corresponding period of 2025, reflecting improved industrial activity amid gradual easing of operating pressures. The performance, according to data from the National Bureau of Statistics (NBS), indicates a gradual recovery in the sector, supported by stronger activities across food and beverages, chemicals, pharmaceuticals, cement and refining subsectors. The improvement was also driven by relative stability in the foreign exchange market, which enhanced manufacturers’ access to imported raw materials and other production inputs, allowing businesses to improve procurement and inventory planning. Similarly, easing inflationary pressures helped reduce uncertainty around input costs, providing some relief to manufacturers and supporting production and business planning. The growth underscores manufacturing’s continued importance to Nigeria’s economic diversification efforts, particularly its role in expanding non-oil production, creating jobs and strengthening domestic value chains. However, despite the improved performance, manufacturers continue to contend with structural challenges, including high energy costs, inadequate infrastructure, logistics bottlenecks and elevated financing costs. These constraints have continued to undermine competitiveness, limit investment capacity and slow production expansion across several industrial segments. The moderation in inflation is expected to provide further relief to businesses and households, potentially supporting consumer demand and enabling manufacturers to plan production more effectively. Nevertheless, persistent geopolitical tensions in the Middle East remain a source of concern for the sector, given their potential implications for global energy prices and supply chains. Any escalation could trigger higher crude oil and gas prices, increase transportation and production costs, and reverse some of the gains from easing domestic inflationary pressures. For Nigerian manufacturers, sustaining the growth momentum will therefore depend not only on macroeconomic stability but also on addressing persistent structural constraints, particularly energy supply, infrastructure deficits and access to affordable financing. The post Manufacturing growth doubles to 3.2% amid easing cost pressures appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: US Airports Expected To Return To Normal Today — Officials
item.description: US air travel was expected to return to normal on Monday after three days of widespread disruption following an extraordinary no-takeoff order issued by US aviation authorities. The ground stop issued Friday afternoon was only the second time such a directive had been issued nationwide in the busy US airspace since planes were grounded following the 9/11 attacks. It was blamed by the Trump administration on a faulty upgrade to communications equipment. As of Sunday evening, more than 55 US-related flights — those traveling within, into or out of the United States — scheduled for Monday were cancelled, according to industry tracker FlightAware. That marked a dramatic shift from the more than 1,960 flights cancelled on Sunday. The Trump administration sought to reassure weary flyers as questions remained over how such chaos could unfold in the world’s largest economy, a country that prides itself on its technological prowess. United Airlines passenger planes are seen at gates at Newark Liberty International Airport (EWR) in Newark, New Jersey, on November 15, 2026. Throughout the weekend, stranded passengers wandered through chaotic airports and sat on floors, waiting for updates or to be rebooked. Officials blamed Friday’s colossal snafu on faulty work to upgrade air traffic control communication cables. President Donald Trump on Sunday ended uncharacteristic days of silence on the ground stop, but only to blame his predecessor Joe Biden for the debacle. Trump insisted he inherited a mess from the Biden administration and said Congress, which his party has controlled for two years, must approve funds to upgrade America’s outdated air traffic control system. “The Biden Administration was an FAA disaster,” Trump said, referring to the Federal Aviation Administration. “Everything they touched turned bad. Big money spent unwisely, making an old and broken system worse than when they began,” Trump asserted. Passengers wait in the terminal of Miami International Airport, Miami on November 13, 2026. FAA chief Bryan Bedford had said Saturday that air travel for millions of Americans stranded at airports would return to normal by the close of business on Sunday. But Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy said Sunday morning it will actually take longer to get planes, crews and travelers to where they need to be. “So, in the airspace, we’re going to see things come back to normal today, but probably fully normal tomorrow,” Duffy said on ABC News. “We had airplanes and crews out of position because of Friday, so it takes a little bit of time to do that.” Passengers wait in line to retrieve their luggage as flights were cancelled at Chicago O’Hare International Airport in Chicago on November 13, 2026. ‘I’m The Secretary’ Duffy also flatly rejected calls for his resignation over the travel chaos, insisting he inherited woefully outdated air traffic control infrastructure, such as, he said, radar equipment that dates back to the 1960s. “So when we do work and thin

item.title: Techie rigged off-spec fan near flammable liquid and an exposed motherboard, then left it to run for days
item.description: If you've made mistakes at work that threatened to torch your career, The Register has just the column for you. We call it Who, Me? , we print one every Monday, and you're reading this week's instalment! Today, meet a reader we'll Regomize as "Axl" who once worked at a petrol station (aka a gas station for US readers). One Friday afternoon, in the shadow of a holiday weekend, the PC that drove the station's pumps and point of sale stopped working, leaving it unable to operate. Axl called the manufacturer and got the very unwelcome news that a technician could visit on Tuesday at the earliest. As the petrol station was in a spot that would attract a few weekend tourists, the potential losses were substantial, and Axl felt he needed to act. He knew the main computer lived inside a large metal box affixed to a wall, an arrangement that meant electronics and flammable vapors were always kept well apart. The machine's power switch was accessible, so Axl turned it off and on again – and watched the machine come back to life, before shutting itself down five minutes later. That behavior was a strong hint that something was overheating but confirming that theory was not easy because the metal case included a lock (see previous remarks about preventing fires) and Axl didn't have they key. Axl inspected the hinges on the box, found they were held on with screws and was able to remove the lid and access the PC. "Aside from the considerable amount of dust and hair inside, I could see that the CPU fan was not turning," he wrote. "Either it had failed or was not receiving the control signal to cool." The service station had an office out the back. Axl liberated a desk fan, pointed it at the PC, and watched it come alive again. An hour later, the PC was still working, so Axl decided he needed a fix that would last the weekend. "I drove to a local electrical shop and purchased a high speed bathroom extraction fan which I rigged up inside the case, then closed it up best I could with tape and cardboard," he told The Register . That rickety rig kept fuel flowing for three days. "On Tuesday afternoon, the support engineer arrived and I explained how I kept us in business over the weekend," Axl wrote. "He just shrugged his shoulders, smiled and changed the failed fan. I didn't even get the 'It's our kit, leave it alone' lecture." He did get the satisfaction of a job well done. "No one died from an exploding petrol station and the tourists were happy they could go home," he wrote. Have you made a risky fix in a dangerous place? If so, the safe option is to click here and send your story to Who, Me? We promise to handle it with care and hopefully share it on some future Monday. ®

item.title: Airline operators, customs agents, others back Tax Ombud, seek fairer tax system
item.description: Dr. Allen Onyema, Vice President of the Airline Operators of Nigeria (AON), has applauded the establishment of the Office of the Tax Ombud, describing it as a significant institutional intervention that provides the aviation sector and taxpayers generally with an impartial platform for resolving complaints and addressing grievances. Delivering a goodwill message at a Town Hall Meeting organised by the Office of the Tax Ombud in Lagos last weekend Onyema highlighted the association’s persistent efforts to draw attention to its grievances at various levels of government, including security and legislative institutions. Onyema made a strong case for the harmonisation of tax regimes to promote fair competition and sustainability, particularly for private and charter airline operators. The Tax Ombud/Chief Executive, Dr. John Nwabueze, said the mandate of his Office includes promoting fairness, transparency and accountability in Nigeria’s tax administration system. He commended President Bola Ahmed Tinubu, for pioneering the establishment of the Office of the Tax Ombud, which is mandated to address operational, administrative and procedural grievances relating to taxes, levies, regulatory fees and customs duties. Nwabueze emphasised that the services of the Office are free of charge to Nigerians, providing an impartial platform for resolving disputes through mediation rather than adversarial proceedings. He further explained that the Office does not determine substantive tax liabilities but focuses on addressing gaps in complaint management and promoting voluntary compliance by building trust between taxpayers and revenue authorities. Underscoring the importance of stakeholder collaboration involving taxpayers, professional associations, business organisations, civil society and the media, he encouraged participants to share their experiences candidly and offer constructive recommendations. Nwabueze, who commended the Minister of Finance and Coordinating Minister of Economy, Mr. Taiwo Oyedele, for his leadership in tax reforms, reassured participants of the Office’s independence and commitment to resolving complaints promptly, reiterating its guiding principle of “bridging differences and building trust.” Engr. Olusola Obadimu, Director-General of the Nigerian Association of Chambers of Commerce, Industry, Mines and Agriculture (NACCIMA), described the Town Hall Meeting as a vital platform for addressing the persistent challenges confronting businesses and industries, ranging from inadequate infrastructure and rising energy costs to the increasing burden of taxation. item.title: Without manufacturing $1tr economy is an illusion
item.description: By Dele Sobowale Japan in fact offers a relevant historical example of what can happen to an economy which falls behind in the global manufacturing race. Even in Africa, the Giant of Africa is lagging behind at least three other economies in the scale and scope of manufacturing. Consequently, the politically-motivated promise to make Nigeria a one trillion dollar economy by 2030 is only one of the many illusions of the Tinubu administration. Desirable as it is, a $1 trillion economy is unachievable for reasons too numerous to discuss now, but, the cardinal reason is Nigeria’s weak manufacturing base – forcing us to import thousands of products which we can, with little effort, produce locally. I was a Senior Lecturer/Consultant working with the Nigerian Institute of Management, NIM, in 1992, when Morita wrote the article in which that statement was made. The NIM Library was my second home and office. When not busy teaching courses in Sales, Marketing and General Management, I was in the Library reading and gathering materials for my lectures, as well as my book of quotations, VBQ – which was published in 2007. Japan was the world’s second largest manufacturing economy as well as the second largest economy; and was threatening the American leadership in that regard. Several books were written on the Art of Japanese Management; leading American Business Schools included courses in Japanese business methods in their curricula as compulsory subjects. The Japanese economy was growing at 7 to 10 per cent annually; and projections were made regarding when it would overtake the US as the largest economy globally. China and India were nowhere in sight. Then, something happened. Science and technology brought new products which called for new and modern factories. Western investors, scared by Japan’s growing economic prowess, diverted investments to other Asian economies – South Korea, Thailand, Malaysia, Indonesia and China. Gradually, several South East Asian nations started challenging Japan in sectors such as electronics and ship building. Unnoticeable at first, but the steady erosion of Japanese share of global manufacturing eventually took its toll. Today, the second and third leading manufacturers are China and India. China is now the largest manufacturer; hotly pursued by China. Japan has dropped to the fifth position in global ranking measured in terms of Gross Domestic Productivity, GDP. China, not Japan, is now threatening the US leadership. Manufacturing is the primary reason for that change in the fortunes of nations. item.title: Dollar to Naira exchange rate today, November 16, 2026
item.description: The Nigerian naira opened Monday, November 16, 2026, under mild pressure across the official Nigerian Foreign Exchange Market (NFEM) while maintaining relative stability in the parallel market. At the official window, data published by the Central Bank of Nigeria (CBN) shows the NFEM rate referencing ₦1,353.97 per dollar. This follows a ₦7.18 depreciation in the preceding session as corporate foreign exchange obligations and seasonal end-of-year import demand weighed on liquidity. Meanwhile, spot interbank indicators in early morning trading hovered around ₦1,343.35 per dollar as dealers awaited fresh intraday price discovery. In the parallel market, also known as the black market, Bureau De Change (BDC) operators and street dealers in Lagos and Abuja quoted the US dollar at a buying rate of ₦1,380 and a selling rate of ₦1,390. With the official rate standing at ₦1,353.97 and the parallel market selling at ₦1,390, the exchange rate spread between both markets sits at approximately ₦36.03 per dollar. Market analysts note that steady foreign reserve buffers and ongoing CBN market interventions continue to keep the disparity between the official and unofficial segments within a narrow band compared to historical volatility. item.title: 1,960 Flights Cancelled On Sunday Alone, As US Airport Disruption Enters Day Three
item.description: An additional 1,960 flights were cancelled on Sunday alone as the widespread disruption following an extraordinary no-takeoff order issued by US aviation authorities entered its third day on Monday. About 6,000 flights were cancelled at the weekend, leaving thousands of passengers stranded at airports. The ground stop issued Friday afternoon was only the second time such a directive had been issued nationwide in the busy US airspace since planes were grounded following the 9/11 attacks. It was blamed by the Trump administration on a faulty upgrade to communications equipment. As of Sunday evening, more than 55 US-related flights — those traveling within, into or out of the United States — scheduled for Monday were cancelled, according to industry tracker FlightAware. That marked a dramatic shift from the more than 1,960 flights cancelled on Sunday. Passengers wait for updates at a check-in area at Terminal 7 at Los Angeles International Airport, in Los Angeles on November 13, 2026. The Trump administration sought to reassure weary flyers as questions remained over how such chaos could unfold in the world’s largest economy, a country that prides itself on its technological prowess. Throughout the weekend, stranded passengers wandered through chaotic airports and sat on floors, waiting for updates or to be rebooked. Officials blamed Friday’s colossal snafu on faulty work to upgrade air traffic control communication cables. President Donald Trump on Sunday ended uncharacteristic days of silence on the ground stop, but only to blame his predecessor Joe Biden for the debacle. Planes sit idle at Los Angeles International Airport in Los Angeles on November 13, 2026. Trump insisted he inherited a mess from the Biden administration and said Congress, which his party has controlled for two years, must approve funds to upgrade America’s outdated air traffic control system. “The Biden Administration was an FAA disaster,” Trump said, referring to the Federal Aviation Administration. “Everything they touched turned bad. Big money spent unwisely, making an old and broken system worse than when they began,” Trump asserted. FAA chief Bryan Bedford had said Saturday that air travel for millions of Americans stranded at airports would return to normal by the close of business on Sunday. But Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy said Sunday morning it will actually take longer to get planes, crews and travelers to where they need to be. “So, in the airspace, we’re going to see things come back to normal today, but probably fully normal tomorrow,” Duffy said on ABC News. “We had airplanes and crews out of position because of Friday, so it takes a little bit of time to do that.” Passengers wait in line to retrieve their luggage as flights were cancelled at Chicago O’Hare International Airport in Chicago on November 13, 2026. ‘I’m The Secretary’ Duffy also flatly rejected calls for his resignation over the travel chaos, insisting he inherited woefully outdated air traffi

item.title: Microsoft’s Azure Linux dons Fedora to dress itself up for mainstream workloads
item.description: Microsoft has issued version 4.0 of its very own Azure Linux, which it built atop Fedora for the first time and now suggests is ready to run mainstream workloads. Redmond’s history with Linux is long and tangled. Former CEO Steve Ballmer infamously labelled the project a cancer but by 2015 Microsoft had quietly adapted the OS to power some switches in its Azure Cloud. Microsoft then built some of its own Azure services on containers and created a lightweight Linux for them to run in. In 2020, Microsoft released that Linux as CBL-Mariner, largely so that developers who used services like Azure Kubernetes Service (AKS) that relied on the OS could access the platform they were building for. In 2022, CBL-Mariner became Azure Linux 2.0, another container-centric lightweight release. Version 3.0 followed in 2024, now billed as ready for “broad Azure usage” with Azure Kubernetes Service. In June 2026, Microsoft announced version 4.0 and billed it as suitable for Azure Virtual Machines, VM Scale Sets, and container images. The big change that made that repositioning possible was basing the OS on Fedora rather than Microsoft’s own Common Base Linux. Microsoft also tuned the Linux kernel – version 6.18 LTS – by adding Hyper-V guest drivers and other features that make it behave well in Azure. It also natively supports tools like Microsoft Defender for Cloud, Azure Monitor, and the Azure CLI, which Microsoft reckons committed Azure users already employ and therefore want to apply to their cloudy Linux workloads. Or as Redmond puts it: “the familiarity of [the] RPM package ecosystem, while adding Azure-native security, compliance, and operational capabilities.” All of those changes add up to an OS that Microsoft says is worth a look “Whether you're running web applications, databases, or GPU-accelerated AI/ML workloads.” Redmond makes that recommendation in part because Azure Linux comes with “no additional OS licensing cost.” Other commercial Linux distributions will cost users money, meaning Microsoft can now make an argument that SUSE and RHEL subscriptions might be superfluous for both AKS users and those who use Azure to host other applications on Linux. Azure Linux 4.0 debuted last Thursday and is available here . Redmond’s latest Linux debuted just days after Microsoft issued a monster upgrade to version 3.0. ®

item.title: Stock market rebounds as investors reap N2.2trn amid decline in oil price
item.description: By Peter Egwuatu The Nigerian stock market rebounded last week after weeks of sustained pressure from profit taking led to decline in stock value. Equity investors on the Nigerian Exchange Limited, NGX, last week, reaped over N2.2 trillion in capital gains leading the NGX market capitalisation, to close last week at N163.795 trillion, up from N161.593 trillion the previous week. Similarly, another major market performance indicator, NGX All Share Index, ASI, surged by 1.4 % to close at 252,269.16 points from 248,877.22 points the previous week, indicating renewed demand for selected heavyweight stocks, which dominated the market. Analysts noted that although buying interests remained evident in major banking and industrial stocks , the broader market reflected a mixed trading pattern, with investors maintaining selective positions amid intermittent profit-taking in several stocks The positive performance, according to analysts, highlights the continued resilience of the domestic stock market, which has maintained substantial gains since the beginning of the year. Reacting to market performance and outlook analysts at InvestData Consulting Limited, said : “ The immediate market outlook remains cautiously positive, supported by the strong year-to-date return and continued interest in selected large-cap stocks. Nevertheless, investors are likely to maintain a selective approach, considering corporate earnings, dividend expectations, valuation levels and prevailing macroeconomic conditions before increasing their exposure. The possibility of further profit-taking cannot be ruled out, particularly in stocks that have recorded significant gains in recent sessions. Overall, the market appears to be consolidating its recent advances while maintaining an underlying bullish bias. The ability of the index to break above the 255,000-point resistance level, alongside improved market participation, will be important in determining whether the current upward movement can extend into another phase of appreciation.” They further noted that the political outcome of the US midterm elections introduced additional uncertainty into the market adding that the developments have placed renewed attention on the possibility of diplomatic negotiations and their implications for global crude supply. “For Nigeria, the movement in international crude prices remains particularly important given the country’s dependence on oil exports for foreign exchange earnings and government revenue. A sustained decline in crude prices could place additional pressure on projected oil receipts, especially if production levels remain below expectations. Conversely, elevated prices could support external earnings, although the benefits would depend on domestic production performance, export volumes and fiscal management” the analysts added. item.title: Imposing Tinubu in 2027 will trigger crisis — Ex-APC spokesman
item.description: ABUJA — FORMER Deputy National Publicity Secretary of the All Progressives Congress, APC, Mr Timi Frank, yesterday, warned that any attempt to force President Bola Tinubu back into office in 2027 could plunge the country into crisis. Read Also: ‘How Tinubu will end insecurity ready’ Frank, who is the Ambassador to East Africa and the Middle East of the United Liberation Movement for West Papua, ULMWP, said Nigerians would not accept an outcome that contradicts their votes. “Nigerians will not accept a situation in which someone is declared the winner when the people know they did not vote for him. They should not push the country into a crisis by attempting to impose him on the people,” he warned. Urging the president to abandon his re-election ambition and guarantee a transparent electoral process, he said: “Whoever wins should be allowed to emerge as the choice of the people.” Frank also expressed concern over alleged attempts by some political actors to manipulate the electoral process. He described the public protest against Tinubu after prayers at the Shehu Shagari Mosque in Area 1, Garki, Abuja, last Friday as evidence of growing dissatisfaction with the administration. Tinubu reportedly faced boos from some Hausa protesters who chanted “Ba ma yi” (we don’t want you) after the prayers. In a viral video, some protesters were seen removing and destroying his campaign posters and billboards in parts of Area 1. Frank condemned the protesters for choosing a religious occasion to vent their displeasure and commended the President’s security detail for ensuring his safety and de-escalating the situation. He nevertheless urged the President to recognise the significance of the public reaction. “The rejection was total and unmistakable. No Nigerian president has been embarrassed like this publicly. The way Nigerians rejected him speaks volumes but should he decide to go ahead and he loses, he should be prepared to accept defeat just like former President Goodluck Jonathan did,” he said. The former APC spokesman said he was worried by what he called a growing gap between the assurances given to the President by political associates and the mood of the people. “I have seen the confidence with which some people are assuring President Tinubu that he will win the Federal Capital Territory, FCT, and that he is firmly in control. But the reported embarrassment he suffered during a prayer session in Abuja tells a different story. “What happened in the FCT last Friday showed that political assurances and promises are not necessarily a reflection of the reality on the ground. The public reaction reflects the anger and dissatisfaction of Nigerians, which those around the President may not be telling him about. “What happened in FCT and Jos after the APC rally has shown that people like the FCT minister, Nyesom Wike promising him 80 percent of votes in Abuja and the Governor of Edo State, Monday Okpebholo vowing to give him 2.5 million votes in Edo State, would

item.title: Economy Palava: Traders decry rising waybill ‘store keep’ charges
item.description: By Elizabeth Adegbesan Small-scale traders operating across major markets in the country have raised the alarm over arbitrary and escalating storage fees, locally known as “store keep money”, charged by transport operators and motor park agents on delayed waybills, warning that the practice is eroding their capital and threatening their livelihoods. For many market women who rely on interstate commercial buses and trucks to restock goods such as foodstuffs, textiles, and household provisions, waybill logistics are the lifeline of daily commerce. However, traders said the shrinking grace periods before daily demurrage charges kick in have turned routine restocking into a financial burden. Economy&Lifestyle visits to some markets revealed a widespread frustration among traders, many of whom operate on thin profit margins and depend on daily turnover or microfinance loans to sustain their stalls. Mrs. Grace Okafor, a wholesale dealer in dried seafood and condiments, recounted how a 24-hour delay caused by heavy rainfall cost her nearly half of her expected profit on a recent consignment. “My goods arrived at the park late in the evening when no one could go out. “By the time I got there the next afternoon with a tricycle to carry my sacks, the park officials insisted I had exceeded their grace period and demanded N6,000 for ‘store keep’. “We cannot increase our selling prices because customers are already struggling to buy. That money came straight out of my capital.” Other traders noted that the lack of standardized billing across motor parks leaves them vulnerable to exploitation, particularly when unforeseen emergencies delay pickup. Mrs. Comfort Momoh, who trades in fabrics and wrappers, stated that arbitrary fee hikes are discouraging traders from ordering goods in bulk. “There is no fixed rate or clear receipt for this store keep money; it depends on the mood of whoever is on duty at the park store,” she said. “Sometimes a driver does not call on time to inform you that the vehicle has arrived, yet the park starts counting storage days against you. By the time you clear your bale, the profit is already gone.” Similarly, Alhaja Rasheedat Suleiman, a palm oil and grain merchant, called on market associations and transport unions to intervene and establish fair, transparent guidelines. “We understand that parks have limited space, but giving traders at least 48 hours of grace after proper notification is only fair,” Alhaja Suleiman said. “Most of us are breadwinners supporting our families from these stalls. If transport companies and park unions do not regulate these charges, many women will be forced out of business.” When contacted, a park supervisor at an interstate loading bay in, who declined to be named, defended the charges, stating that limited warehouse space and the risk of theft or damage make it necessary to compel traders to clear their goods promptly. item.title: More deaths, abductions in Zamfara, Sokoto
item.description: Bandits have killed Nasiru Sani Kaura, a Senior Special Assistant to Zamfara State Governor, Dauda Lawal, in Kaura Namoda town. The governor’s aide was shot dead when bandits attacked the Low Cost area of Kaura Namoda in the early hours of Sunday. In Sokoto State, gunmen attacked Yartsakuwa community in Rabah Local Government Area on Saturday, killing three people and abducting 22, mostly women. Witnesses said the attackers stormed the community at night and took away the victims. State police: Senate asks remaining assemblies to submit report tomorrow Electoral Act provision on ballot papers sparks fresh debate The latest attacks came a few days after more than 30 suspected bandits and seven members of a local vigilante group were reportedly killed during a clash in Zauma community, Bukkuyum LGA of Zamfara State. Meanwhile, security agencies recorded some successes in operations against bandits and terrorists in the two states. Speaking on the attack in Kaura Namoda, Zamfara, residents said the gunmen stormed the neighbourhood while Muslims were observing the early morning (Subh) prayer, shooting sporadically and forcing people to flee for safety. Nasiru, a grassroots politician and community leader, was killed during the attack. One of the worshippers, who witnessed the incident, told Daily Trust that the attackers arrived while the imam was reciting Qur’an during the second rak’ah of the prayer. He said the late Sani was standing in the back row of the congregation when the gunmen entered the mosque. “We were observing congregational prayer when our imam was reciting the surah in the second rak’ah of the Fajr prayer. Suddenly, the attackers stormed the mosque. “Hon. Sani tried to escape. He was wearing a big attire, and when one of the bandits grabbed him, he removed the attire and ran. Unfortunately, when he got outside, he met another bandit who was positioned near the garden, apparently to intercept anyone escaping. The man shot him,” the witness said. Another worshipper said panic erupted when someone entered the mosque and alerted the congregation that bandits had invaded the area. “Everybody immediately scattered and started running for safety,” he said. A resident, who spoke to Daily Trust on condition of anonymity, said the attackers abducted nine people but later released four children, leaving five persons in their custody. He said the five abducted persons comprised four young men and an elderly man. According to him, some residents subsequently rushed to their houses, collected their weapons and pursued the attackers but could not catch up with them. Another resident said he was among the first people to return to the scene to assist the late governor’s aide after the attackers fled, but found him dead. The Zamfara State Police Command spokesperson, DSP Yazid Abubakar, confirmed the killing of one person in the attack. item.title: APOD: 2026 November 16 – NGC 7129: Star Formation with Jets from Webb
item.description: APOD Science APOD APOD: 2026 November 16 – NGC… Today’s APOD Archive Submissions Index Search Calendar RSS Education About Discuss APOD Astronomy Picture of the Day Discover the cosmos! Each day a different image or photograph of our fascinating universe is featured, along with a brief explanation written by a professional astronomer. NGC 7129: Star Formation with Jets from Webb Explanation: How do stars form? To help answer this question, NASA used the James Webb Space Telescope to take the featured detailed image of the star-forming region NGC 7129 in infrared light . Star formation progresses when gravity pulls together massive amounts of gas, but soon things can get complicated when previously formed stars emit powerful jets and winds — and some then explode . Opaque dust can form in the cool atmospheres of stars and, when dispersed, can obstruct visible-light images. Many stars can be seen to be forming in the featured image , with the young stars on the left, in the gold-colored gas, typically being more mature than the young stars on the right — in the red region. Jets and wind s likely cause the filamentary nature of the red-colored gas. Studying stars at different stages of development bolsters understanding about what physical processes are most important and when. item.description: Earth Observatory Science Earth Observatory The Last Ice on Puncak Jaya Earth Earth Observatory Image of the Day EO Explorer Topics All Topics Atmosphere Land Heat & Radiation Life on Earth Human Dimensions Natural Events Oceans Remote Sensing Technology Snow & Ice Water More Content Collections Global Maps World of Change Articles Earth Matters Blog Blue Marble: Next Generation EO Kids Mission: Biomes About About Us Subscribe 🛜 RSS Contact Us Search 1988 2026 A false-color satellite image from 1988 shows mountain ridges of Indonesia’s Sudirman Range. Bare rock appears brown, and glacial ice, shown in blue, caps several of the highest ridges. Vegetation at lower elevations appears green. NASA Earth Observatory / Lauren Dauphin A false-color satellite image shows the same area in 2026. Only a few small fragments of ice remain, shown in blue, and bare brown rock covers most of the ridgetops that were icy in 1988. NASA Earth Observatory / Lauren Dauphin 1988 2026 A false-color satellite image from 1988 shows mountain ridges of Indonesia’s Sudirman Range. Bare rock appears brown, and glacial ice, shown in blue, caps several of the highest ridges. Vegetation at lower elevations appears green. NASA Earth Observatory / Lauren Dauphin A false-color satellite image shows the same area in 2026. Only a few small fragments of ice remain, shown in blue, and bare brown rock covers most of the ridgetops that were icy in 1988. NASA Earth Observatory / Lauren Dauphin 1988 2026 Curtain Toggle 2-Up On the island of New Guinea, Indonesia’s Sudirman Range is one of the few places near the equator that have long held ice year-round. But near the summit of Puncak Jaya, the ice has dwindled to patches too small to flow like glaciers. Positioned in the tropics beside the largest expanse of warm ocean water on Earth, the range’s glaciers lie near the warmest conditions in which ice can survive year-round. Scientists have described these glaciers as high-altitude “ canaries in the coal mine ,” alongside other tropical ice such as the remnants of Humboldt Glacier in Venezuela, Quelccaya Ice Cap in Peru, and the ice fields of Kilimanjaro in Tanzania. The change on Puncak Jaya is visible in this image pair, acquired in 1988 by the TM (Thematic Mapper) on Landsat 5 (left) and in 2026 by the OLI (Operational Land Imager) on Landsat 9 (right). The false-color images help distinguish areas of ice (light blue) from exposed bedrock (brown). Clouds appear white and vegetation green. In 1988, the glaciers covered about 4.31 square kilometers (1.66 square miles), according to Donaldi Permana, a climate scientist at the Indonesian Agency for Meteorology, Climatology, and Geophysics (BMKG). By September 2025, satellite and aerial data showed that only about 0.09 square kilometers (0.03 square miles) remained—an area equivalent to about a dozen soccer fields. That’s roughly 2 percent of the 1988 extent. An aerial survey planned for December should yield an estimate of how much ice remain

item.title: Crisis hits Nigeria’s cassava industry with imports rising 13,293% in 5yrs
item.description: *… as Farmers Abandon Farms in 2026 By Cynthia Alo Nigeria’s cassava processing industry is facing a deepening crisis as imports of cassava starch surged by 13,293 per cent in five years, leaving local factories struggling, farmers counting their losses and processors operating at low 15 per cent of their installed capacity. This is happening despite Nigeria’s position as the world’s largest cassava producer as of 2024, according to the Food and Agriculture Organization Corporate Statistical Database, FAOSTAT, an agency of the United Nations. Industry stakeholders attributed the crisis to high production costs, inadequate financing, declining farm acreage and weak enforcement of import restrictions. These factors have made imported alternatives cheaper than locally produced cassava derivatives. The situation has resulted in a glut of raw cassava, falling farm-gate prices, mounting debts among farmers and processors, and growing concerns about the future of local industrial production. Data obtained from the World Bank’s World Integrated Trade Solution, WITS, based on UN Comtrade records, showed that Nigeria’s cassava starch imports rose from 24.1 tonnes in 2020 to 3,227.7 tonnes in 2025, representing a 13,293 per cent increase over five years. A year-on-year breakdown showed that Nigeria imported 24.1 tonnes of cassava starch, valued at $69,440, in 2020. Imports increased by 126.6 per cent year-on-year (YoY) in 2021 to 54.6 tonnes, worth $154,750. In 2022, the volume surged by a further 272.2 per cent YoY to 203.2 tonnes, valued at $292,900. However, following a sharp rise in the exchange rate, imports plunged by 98 per cent YoY in 2023 to 4.1 tonnes, valued at $32,080, before rebounding sharply in 2024 by 73,004.9 per cent to 2,997.3 tonnes, worth $2.34 million. The upward trend continued in 2025, with import volumes rising by 7.7 per cent to 3,227.7 tonnes. However, despite the increase in volume, the value of imports declined by 7.6 per cent to $2.16 million from approximately $2.34 million in 2024. Industry stakeholders, who spoke in exclusive interviews with Financial Vanguard, warned that imports were rising further in 2026 and could continue to increase in subsequent years unless the government addressed the cost disadvantages confronting local processors and strengthened policies supporting domestic production. Farmers, processors count losses The President of Large-Scale Starch and Derivatives Producers Association of Nigeria, LSSDPA, Mrs Oluyemisi Iranloye, who is also the Vice-President of the Industrial Cassava Stakeholders Association of Nigeria, ICSAN, said the crisis had severely affected farmers and processors. Iranloye, founder and Chief Executive Officer of Psaltry International, said farmers could spend about N800,000 cultivating a hectare of cassava but realise only about N300,000 from selling the produce at prevailing farm-gate prices. She said the situation had discouraged farmers from planting, while industrial processors,

item.title: Igini to Trump: Tie Nigeria-US relations to credible polls
item.description: A former Independent National Electoral Commission, INEC, Resident Electoral Commissioner, Mike Igini, has urged US President, Donald Trump, to link America’s immigration policy and diplomatic relations with Nigeria to credible conduct of the country’s 2027 general elections. Read Also: ‘How Tinubu will end insecurity ready’ Igini said electoral malpractice, corruption, insecurity and poor governance were among the factors forcing Nigerians to seek opportunities abroad, arguing that credible elections and accountable leadership could help address the root causes of migration. In an open letter dated November 13, 2026, and addressed to Trump at the White House, the former REC proposed a policy he called the “No Mandate Fraud” Doctrine, urging the US to combine preventive diplomacy, independent election monitoring and targeted sanctions against individuals involved in electoral violations. He argued that border enforcement alone could not address migration without tackling the governance failures driving Nigerians out of their country. “Nigerians are not leaving Nigeria because they do not love their country. They are leaving because of decades of persistent electoral malpractice, corruption, insecurity and weak public accountability that have undermined Nigerians’ confidence in government,” he wrote. Igini urged Trump to send a high-level delegation to engage President Bola Tinubu, political parties, presidential and governorship candidates, INEC and other relevant institutions ahead of the elections. He said the delegation should communicate Washington’s position that credible elections, peaceful political competition and respect for constitutional rights were central to US interests in Nigeria. He also proposed visa restrictions, financial sanctions and asset freezes, where legally justified, against electoral officials found culpable of manipulating results, falsifying records or committing other electoral offences. The former REC extended the call for accountability to judicial officers whose misconduct in electoral cases was established by credible evidence, as well as security personnel involved in voter intimidation, electoral violence and suppression of opposition parties. He identified the police, Department of State Services, Armed Forces and Nigeria Security and Civil Defence Corps as institutions expected to protect voters and ensure impartial enforcement of the law. Igini further urged the US to support credible domestic and international election observers to monitor the process before, during and after the polls, particularly voter intimidation, security neutrality, polling-unit results and transparent collation. Explaining the benefits to Washington, he said credible elections could reduce migration pressure, strengthen security cooperation and create opportunities for stronger economic relations. He also identified potential US investment in Nigeria’s energy sector, particularly electricity development, through technology transfer

item.title: We demand impeccable voter register
item.description: The Independent National Electoral Commission, INEC, must urgently clean up its battered image by producing an impeccable voters’ register ahead of the 2027 general elections. The discovery that its own officials allegedly compromised the database through fraudulent registrations is a monumental embarrassment. It reinforces existing suspicions about the commission’s impartiality and competence at a time Nigerians desperately need an electoral umpire they can trust. The scale of the problem is alarming. Of the more than 11 million people registered during the 2026 Continuous Voter Registration, CVR, exercise, INEC’s Automated Biometric Identification System, ABIS, flagged approximately 1.5 million entries as suspicious. The commission subsequently removed 1,277,252 invalid records, leaving about 268,000 requiring further verification. The preliminary national register contains over 103.4 million voters. More disturbing is the alleged complicity of registration officers who abused their official login credentials to introduce fictitious identities. They reportedly uploaded AI-generated photographs, reused identical images and exploited registration provisions for persons with disabilities, claiming fictitious applicants had no fingers and could therefore bypass normal fingerprint verification. ABIS detected suspicious facial and biometric inconsistencies during screening. Artificial intelligence has consequently introduced a dangerous dimension toa electoral fraud. Its capacity to generate convincing human faces makes fabricating identities easier and visual inspection less reliable. Although digitally enhanced photographs of genuine applicants are not necessarily fraudulent, fictitious identities must be identified and eliminated. INEC says it has withdrawn implicated officers’ access credentials, commenced investigations, subjected suspicious entries to human adjudication and referred evidence for possible disciplinary action and prosecution. It promises further verification before the final register is displayed on December 15, 2026. These assurances are insufficient without demonstrable accountability. Public confidence in INEC was already fragile before this scandal. Controversies surrounding previous elections, particularly the disputed 2023 presidential election and the failure of IReV to upload results as expected, have deepened distrust. A manipulated register could facilitate fictitious voting identities, impersonation, inflated constituency figures and deliberate disenfranchisement of legitimate voters. Biometric accreditation may prevent some abuses, but cannot excuse a defective database. Professor JoashAmupitan must therefore open the corrective process to independent scrutiny. INEC should partner with opposition parties, civil society organisations, professional technology experts, the media and credible international electoral partners in conducting an independent forensic audit. The commission should publish state-by-state findings

item.title: ASUU Heroes Day, 2027 elections and the futuristic State Police, by Owei Lakemfa
item.description: It was one of the largest gatherings of Africa’s best brains. The date was November 12, the Academic Staff Union of Universities (ASUU) 2026 Heroes Day. The academics came from all parts of the country, gathering at the University of Abuja. Amongst them were current and former vice-chancellors, current and past presidents of ASUU, and founding NLC President, Comrade Hassan Sunmonu. There was Alhaji Mahmud Yayale Ahmed, who has held three of the country’s highest public offices: Secretary to the Government of the Federation, Head of the Civil Service, and Minister of Defence. Former Bauchi State Governor AhmaduAdamuMu’azu, ex-Permanent Secretaries Professor GokeAdegoroye and Dr. TimiebiKoripamo-Agary, who, as serving Permanent Secretary, Ministry of Labour and Productivity, sued a Minister for conduct bordering on corruption. Minister of State SuwaibaSa’idu Ahmad, a professor of Science Education, held herself up as a proud member of ASUU, identified the principle of good welfare for academics, and urged all to continuously help build bridges between Government and ASUU. The occasion embodied three primary characteristics of the seventy-eight-year-old ASUU. First, ever analysing the past, which is why it annually marks its Heroes Day to honour those who have made sacrifices for the union, universities, and the country. The Day commemorates November 12, 2013, the date former ASUU President and noted novelist Festus Iyayi was killed in a car crash. He was travelling for an ASUU National Executive Council meeting in Kano to find a solution to a national strike triggered by Government’s intransigence and insistence on defunding education. The second ASUU culture is ever interrogating the present, which is why this year’s theme focused on the electoral system. The third is the union’s tendency to probe into the future. This time, it looked at the ongoing attempts to create State Police and the possible impact it could have on the 2027 General Elections. ASUU is also quite strategic in building alliances, which is why its awardees this year included a number of people who led the Government Negotiating Teams or played roles in ensuring the success of the decades-long ASUU-Government negotiations. These included Alhaji Ahmed, Professor MunzaliJibril, whose Negotiating Team in May 2021 broke through barriers and successfully produced a draft agreement, and Professor NimiDimkpa Briggs, who, on June 16, 2022, despite government reservations, followed through with a new draft agreement within ten weeks. The Buhari government had been so displeased with the breakthrough the Briggs Team had made with ASUU that it made false accusations against the likeable professor. It accused him of excluding government agencies from the negotiations, inflating academics’ salaries by N1.1 trillion, and acting out of financial self-interest. item.title: Nigeria: One-party or one-man state? By Suleiman A. Suleiman
item.description: Since at least late 2024, when President Bola Ahmed Tinubu had been in office for barely 18 months, politicians and other Nigerians have been saying that the country is drifting into a one-party state. These warnings have not only grown louder in recent months; they are justified. The All Progressives Congress (APC) now controls 31 out of 36 states, since at least the middle of this year, when the 2027 election campaigns entered top gear. At the end of the 2023 election cycle, the APC controlled 21 states, including the off-cycle election in Edo State in 2024. This means that, in the last year, 10 sitting governors have defected from their original parties to join Tinubu in the APC. The reverse traffic, meanwhile, is zero. This is unlike the 2015 election cycle, when leading politicians were defecting from the then ruling People’s Democratic Party (PDP) to the then main opposition APC. At the same time, the transformation of political organisation and opposition parties that we witnessed during 2013–2015 does not appear to be happening this time, as the leading opposition parties remain ridden by crippling crises that President Tinubu and the APC have been accused of instigating. First of all, the PDP is now a one-man show, and it is difficult to even know what the party stands for or who its leading members are, other than FCT Minister Nyesom Wike. More significantly, in 2023, the Labour Party (LP) and the New Nigeria Peoples Party (NNPP) won 63 seats between them—almost all of them for the first time in history—in the National Assembly elections, and a total of 12 states and the FCT in the presidential election by their candidates, Mr Peter Obi and Dr Rabiu Kwankwaso, combined. That was a formidable performance, particularly by Peter Obi, but both the LP and the NNPP are no longer serious contenders in this election, and the two men have since left to meet on the same presidential ticket in the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC). Accusing fingers also point to Tinubu for making their own political parties unviable platforms for the two men. This leaves the African Democratic Congress (ADC), which faces the most crisis of all. For almost a year, the ADC, formed by a partial coalition of like-minded and opposition interests, has been held hostage by the antics of one man, enabled almost entirely by Nigerian courts. The status of ADC candidates, from the presidential to the state assembly elections, currently hangs in limbo because Nigerian courts in this era now think that the dubious concerns of one party member are more important than the will of all the voters in the hundreds of primary elections conducted by the APC in the past months. In short, Nigeria today looks like a one-party state, with the ruling APC as the last man standing. In my view, however, Nigeria is not sliding into a one-party state. It is already a one-man state. A one-party state—a country where a single political party dominates the political space—is a form of authoritaria

item.title: PenCom opens up on N52,000 minimum pension guarantee
item.description: By Victor Ahiuma-Young The National Pension Commission, PenCom, has shed light on the implementation of the long-awaited Minimum Pension Guarantee, MPG, disclosing that 173,209 Nigerian retirees are eligible to benefit from a guaranteed minimum monthly pension of N52,500 following its formal activation by President Bola Tinubu. The initiative, aimed at improving the welfare and financial security of retirees under the Contributory Pension Scheme, CPS, was unveiled alongside a healthcare programme designed to provide free access to essential medical services for low-income pensioners. The two initiatives, the Minimum Pension Guarantee and the Pension Industry Healthcare Plan (PenCare), were announced at the Presidential Pension Security Initiatives ceremony held at the State House Banquet Hall, Abuja. Tinubu, who was represented at the event by Senate President Godswill Akpabio, said the Minimum Pension Guarantee fulfilled a provision of the Pension Reform Act 2004, which was retained in the 2014 legislation but had remained unimplemented for 22 years. Declaring the scheme operational, the President assured pension contributors that the government would no longer allow eligible retirees to receive pensions below the guaranteed minimum threshold. “From this day, there is a floor beneath the Nigerian retiree. No one who contributed under the Contributory Pension Scheme will ever be allowed to fall below,” he said. The President urged successive administrations to sustain the policy and periodically increase the guaranteed amount rather than discontinue it. On the healthcare component, President Tinubu said the Pension Industry Healthcare Plan, PenCare, was designed to shield vulnerable retirees from medical expenses that could deplete their retirement savings. He said beneficiaries would receive healthcare access cards in the coming months, enabling them to access essential medical services without bearing the financial burden. The President also disclosed that his administration had issued a N758 billion bond to address outstanding pension arrears and approved a N32,000 monthly consequential adjustment for affected federal pensioners. He added that state governments had collectively spent more than N1 trillion settling outstanding pension obligationsSpeaking at the ceremony, PenCom Director-General, Omolola Oloworaran, disclosed that 173,209 retirees had qualified for the N52,500 monthly minimum pension. She explained that the beneficiaries comprised 34 per cent of retirees from federal service, 12 per cent from state employment and 54 per cent from the private sector. According to her, the guaranteed amount was determined through actuarial validation and would be reviewed periodically to ensure its sustainability. item.title: Amazon loses first batch of broadband satellites launched on custom rocket
item.description: Amazon’s ambition to operate a constellation of broadband satellites took a hit on Sunday, when 40 of its craft failed to make it into orbit. The failure is significant because it was the first Amazon launch to use a rocket designed especially for the job of carrying its broadband birds to low Earth orbit. The Lockheed/Boeing joint venture United Launch Alliance (ULA) created that rocket, a version of its Vulcan heavy lifter using a six-booster configuration and a Centaur V upper stage optimized to carry payloads into low Earth orbit. Last week, Amazon previewed the launch with a post that noted this mission, code-named LV-01, is the first of 38 planned missions with ULA, and that LV-02 would likely follow within weeks. The two companies planned to test new hardware on the first “several” flights using the custom rocket. Amazon put 40 satellites aboard the Sunday mission and said it is “already planning larger configurations for subsequent missions.” Those plans, and the LV-02 launch, are probably on hold after the rocket suffered an anomaly 10 minutes into the flight. The flight began well, with the Vulcan reaching an altitude of 95 miles (150 km) and completing the first phase of its flight. Six minutes into the mission, the main booster and payload fairing both separated as planned, and ULA lit up the Centaur V’s engines for the first planned firings needed to reach low Earth orbit. Then came the anomaly, which UAL’s live update stream states meant the mission “failed to deliver the Amazon mission to orbit.” “Every flight generates data, and every flight teaches us something,” UAL wrote. “Since the anomaly just occurred, we don’t have any specific data yet to understand what occurred today.” Amazon already has over 200 satellites in orbit, had hoped to launch its satellite broadband service this year, and plans 20 or more launches in 2027. It is unclear if this mission failure will change those ambitions. ®

item.title: Development challenges in Delta: Ebitonmo’s theory of political thermodynamics
item.description: By Enewaridideke Ekanpou Alapala Anthony Ebitonmo, the man currently representing Burutu North Constituency in the Delta State House of Assembly, is again furious, as it is his wont to be, resistant to every benevolent arrester unleashed on him. Rather retrospectively, in a blazing fury, he was recently sighted at Oyangbene and approvingly led into the open arms of people carrying “chalked hearts.” The hearts of Oyangbene people became immediately “chalked” because Ebitonmo was suddenly sighted. Even in their variedly chalked hearts at the sight of the man, they were confounded, thrown off balance, when they were told he had not come for Oyangbene community. Even in their confoundment, they sought to know the rationale behind Ebitonmo’s sudden appearance in Oyangbene when he claimed openly he had not come for the Oyangbene community. In a characteristic blazing fury, he was curtly categorical that his sudden appearance was rooted in two propellants—Serikoromo Primary School and his famed theory named political thermodynamics. Available statistics reveal Serikoromo Primary School in Burutu Local Government Area of Delta State had been the home of rickety structures for decades, daily rendezvoused by pythons, leopards, elephants, lions, grasscutters, lizards, iguanas, rats, cats, and bats. To teachers and pupils, these reptiles and mammals became the bandits troubling them. For decades, they cried their eyes out with tears that spread like the waters of the Atlantic Ocean. However, their impassioned tears looked like the silvery waters in the ocean; they were not comforted like the weeping Biblical Martha. Serikoromo Primary School, founded in 1956, was where I had my primary education in 1988. The oceanic tears of this school had known many decades of neglect. Awakened to the pathetic story of Serikoromo Primary School, Ebitonmo became blazingly furious. With a blazing fury that carried the troubling pains of the poor teachers and pupils, Ebitonmo risked a sudden flight to Serikoromo Primary School without a visible speedboat professionally skimming the white waters of Oyangbene River. His presence in the school was equivalent to ritualistically stepping on “Atu” in a folktale stunningly told by TimiebiMaika. Mystically, as captured in Timiebi’s folktales, ritualistically stepping on the “Atu” was imbued with the power to make one appear dramatically at the backyard of one’s house. The power of invisibility and disappearance dwells mystically in the “Atu” ritual. The second propellant of Ebitonmo’s appearance in Oyangbene without a visible flight was his treasured philosophy of political thermodynamics. Political thermodynamics is the measurable degree of responsiveness of, or applicability of, core developmental ideas to visible development challenges that plague communities and mankind in general. It is the space for the transformation of strategically formulated developmental ideas into enduring visible structures through the interrogative inte

item.title: Microsoft lifts Indian cloud prices by 15 percent, cuts costs in China
item.description: Microsoft has announced massive price rises for commercial cloud services in India and New Zealand, but a substantial reduction in China. The software giant sells its cloudy services in many local currencies, at an equivalent rate to the prices it charges in the USA. As exchange rates shift, so do the prices Microsoft charges around the world. Microsoft last week announced the new charges that will come into effect from January 1, 2027, and the news isn’t pleasant for customers in India, who face an increase of 15.7 percent for cloud services and up to 20 percent for some on-prem offerings. New Zealand customers face a ten percent price hike. Customers in China, where Microsoft relies on a local partner called 21Vianet to deliver its cloud, will see costs fall by up to 8.5 percent. Australian buyers will see costs fall by 4.5 percent. The only nation not in Asia on Microsoft’s list is Norway, where prices will ease 5.9 percent. Sega Japan hits double trouble Sega has just had a rotten week that saw it battle a data leak and an outage. The outage impacted the company’s ALL.Net and Aime services, which connect arcade games across different locations. The services include administrative features for arcade operators, plus services for gamers including pre-payment to play, high score and profile recording, and networked gaming. Sega suspended some ALL.Net and Aime services on November 1 after discovering unauthorized access to servers. At least thirteen games and services were then unavailable until around November 15. The company hasn’t explained what went wrong, but assured customers the incident was not a data breach and that payment information was safe. But data did leak for those who subscribe to some Sega newsletters. Sega uses a third-party outfit called Arara Co. to send some emails, and it leaked email addresses. No other personal data leaked from Arara. Sega has nonetheless warned newsletter recipients to watch out for suspicious messages. Alibaba floats chip unit Chinese tech giant Alibaba last week announced its intention to float its T-Head chip design biz on the Hong Kong Stock Exchange. The filing announcing the spinoff describes T-Head as “a leading provider of full-stack data center chips which enable system-level compute solutions in China,” suggesting Alibaba doesn’t think buyers in the rest of the world are keen to acquire its chips. T-Head going public “allows a more efficient deployment of Alibaba Group’s financial resources,” the filing states, and should also mean the chip design outfit can more easily find third-party customers. India bans export of dead batteries The government of India last week banned the export of “Lithium-Ion battery Black Mass” – a powdery substance created during the process of recycling batteries. “It contains recoverable quantities of critical minerals, including lithium, cobalt, nickel and manganese,” according to the government’s announcement of the ban, which argues the measure “will increase dom

item.title: Vulcan rocket fails during launch, dealing major blow to SpaceX competitors
item.description: United Launch Alliance's Vulcan rocket and 40 Amazon Leo broadband satellites fell back to Earth minutes after liftoff Sunday, a crushing setback that will ripple across all sectors of the US space industry. The Vulcan rocket is on contract to launch roughly half of the US military's national security space missions in the next few years, and Sunday's mission was the first of 38 Vulcan launches booked by Amazon to build out its network of broadband Internet satellites aimed at competing with SpaceX's Starlink. Sunday's failure is expected to ground the rocket for an indefinite period of time. Vulcan is no stranger to close calls, having overcome failures with its strap-on solid rocket boosters on two of its four previous flights. In each case, the rocket corrected for those problems and continued into orbit to deploy its payloads. The incidents trigged months-long reviews and investigations before ULA could resume Vulcan flights. Read full article Comments

item.title: England End Spain’s 44-Game Unbeaten Run With Nations League Win
item.description: England snapped world champions Spain’s unbeaten run with a 3-2 victory in Madrid on Sunday to clinch the top spot in Nations League group A3. Goals from Harry Kane, Ezri Konsa and Ben White inflicted La Roja’s first loss in a competitive game since March 2023, after 44 without defeat. England’s Elliot Anderson was sent off in the second half as Spain fought back from three goals down with strikes from Mikel Oyarzabal and Nico Williams, but Luis de la Fuente’s World Cup winners could not find the equaliser. Both sides were already sure to progress, but as group winners England will be seeded for the quarter-finals in March. England coach Thomas Tuchel selected James Trafford in goal over Jordan Pickford and also brought White and Konsa into the side. Teenage star Lamine Yamal was fit to start for Spain at Atletico Madrid’s Metropolitano stadium after missing their midweek win over the Czech Republic. However the youngster did not see much of the ball in the first half as England came out strongly. Spain’s midfielder #09 Fermin Lopez challenges England’s goalkeeper #13 James Trafford during the UEFA Nations League – League A day 6 group 3 – football match between Spain and England at Metropolitano Stadium in Madrid on November 15, 2026. (Photo by Thomas COEX / AFP) Spain goalkeeper Unai Simon produced a strong reaction save to deny Jude Bellingham, while Anthony Gordon had a dangerous shot blocked. Ballon d’Or winner Kane, who beat Yamal to the award, sent an effort narrowly wide. Barcelona defender Pau Cubarsi handed England the advantage when he clumsily felled Kane in the area on the stroke of half time. The Bayern Munich hitman powered a perfect penalty past Simon, who dived the right way but to no avail. De la Fuente tried to react at half-time with a triple change, including throwing on Barcelona duo Fermin Lopez and Pedri, but England quickly found more joy. England’s midfielder #17 Morgan Rogers fights for the ball with Spain’s forward #17 Nico Williams during the UEFA Nations League – League A day 6 group 3 – football match between Spain and England at Metropolitano Stadium in Madrid on November 15, 2026. (Photo by Javier SORIANO / AFP) Konsa headed home the second from Declan Rice’s corner in the 53rd minute after the Arsenal defender was left unmarked by Spain’s defence. Four minutes later England sliced open Spain’s defence with Kane and Bellingham combining to set up White for the third. La Roja clawed their way back into the game when Elliot Anderson fouled Yamal in the area as the Spain striker ran in on goal. The Manchester City midfielder was dismissed and Mikel Oyarzabal slotted home the penalty. Spain found a second when Gordon gave the ball away and Yamal fed Nico Williams, whose shot hit the post and bounced in. Williams curled over and Trafford denied Yamal and Marc Cucurella as Spain looked fruitlessly for the goal they needed to preserve their unbeaten record. item.title: 30 years ago, 'Space Jam' proposed the best way to resolve interplanetary disputes
item.description: null You just ordered a Pizza Hut and a two-liter bottle of Mountain Dew. You put on "Space Jam" to watch the greatest of all time team up with the Looney Tunes. It's a perfect evening… in 1996 or 2026. The entire concept of "Space Jam" is so '90s that you swear you can hear Los Del Rio in the background mouthing, "Dale a tu cuerpo alegría, Macarena." As ridiculous as an intergalactic basketball match may sound, it's a perfect example of how even the strangest idea can work if you commit to it fully. In case you thought you hallucinated the whole thing, no, you didn't, as the Looney Tunes find themselves in quite the predicament in this live-action-animation hybrid. A bunch of aliens known as the Nerdlucks arrive on Earth to abduct the Tunes and take them back as attractions to the outer-space amusement park known as Moron Mountain (shockingly nobody has claimed that subreddit, so do your thing, Internet!). Being a wheeling-and-dealing wabbit, though, Bugs Bunny proposes a winner-takes-all basketball game between the Tunes and the tiny Nerdlucks. Unfortunately, the crafty aliens use their tech to steal the talent from ballers like Charles Barkley and Muggsy Bogues and turn themselves into the scary and skilled Monstars. So, Bugs and friends reach out to Michael Jordan, who recently switched from basketball to baseball, to help the Tune Squad win this intergalactic b-ball matchup and their freedom, because if anybody can do it, Air Jordan (Hare Jordan?) can. Oh, Bill Murray also shows up here a few times. Why? Because he can! (Image credit: Warner Bros. Pictures) "Space Jam" is a spin on the classic sci-fi trope of resolving high-stakes conflicts through sports. In 1975, "Death Race 2000" introduced a world where people drive like hooligans and bash into each other to get ahead and win races (ironically, this is the regular experience on any public road now). Meanwhile, in the same year, "Rollerball" demonstrated how to use extreme sports as a plot device whereby brutality trumped any kind of skill in the arena. Yet "Space Jam" took this concept, cartoonified it for a family-friendly audience, and challenged the conflict resolution approaches of other alien invasion movies from 1996. While " Independence Day " saw the heroes trying to destroy the mothership and "Mars Attacks" featured humans running away from "Ack! Ack"-ing extraterrestrials with ray guns, this film used the court to settle the score. It's an innovative way to deal with interplanetary matters, that's for sure. (Image credit: Warner Bros Pictures) Here's the thing: a basketball game is incredibly fair and puts everybody on equal footing. It isn't about who has the biggest guns or most high-tech spacecraft; it's about who can best work as a team to get a result. Now, this isn't to say that the Looney Tunes and Nerdlucks ever planned on playing by the rules. item.title: On this day in space! Nov. 15, 1988: The 300-foot Green Bank Telescope collapses suddenly, leaving a huge pile of wreckage in West Virginia
item.description: null On Nov. 15, 1988, a 300-foot radio telescope in Green Bank, West Virginia suddenly collapsed. It happened at 9:46 p.m. on a clear night with no strong winds. When the observatory staff showed up to work the next morning, they were greeted by a huge pile of wreckage. The telescope collapsed under its own weight after a key structural element called a "gusset plate" failed. This was one of four connecting plates that held the telescope's large, metal beams together. Investigators found that these gusset plates were not built to last the 26 years that this telescope had been in use. Three years later, construction began on a new telescope. The Green Bank Telescope was even bigger and more sensitive, and it began science operations in 2001. (Image credit: NRAO/AUI/NSF) Why it mattered When the 300-foot telescope first debuted, it was not just the United States' largest radio observatory, but the largest such facility in the world. But its quick construction — just two years — led to it having to be significantly upgraded later. "In 1970, the 300-foot’s surface had become so warped from maintenance crews, snow, and its own weight that a new finer-meshed aluminum surface was installed," the website for the National Radio Astronomy Observatory reads. "A larger traveling feed was also installed at the prime focus." The collapse, however, was no one's fault. "Unforeseeable stress factors cracked a steel connector plate," wrote the NRAO. The Green Bank Telescope collapse left a mass of twisted debris behind. (Image credit: NRAO/AUI/NSF) During its years of observations, the 300-foot telescope contirbuted to the discovery of dark matter and the realization that pulsars come from supernova explosions. "One of the most important products to come out of the 300-foot telescope was an all-sky survey of radio objects called the Green Bank 6cm Survey. Nearly every northern hemisphere radio object studied by any other telescope is from a catalog compiled using this telescope," reads the NRAO website. Want more space history? Check out our full On This Day In Space Story archive and watch our On This Day In Space videos on YouTube .
